2. What Is a BFS Level Queue?
C → CA → CAT → CATS (dead end, back up)
CPU waits on each memory read in turn
& mispredicts when paths hit dead ends
BFS Queue: Grow All Paths 1 Step!
Why It's Fast: Parallel Memory Reads!
Paths in a row don't depend on each other,
so the CPU fetches their Trie nodes at once.
Each Queue Item Is Just 8 Bytes:
squares this path already stepped on
How Bitmasks Find Valid Next Squares
Bit 2 ('T') and Bit 5 ('R') continue a valid word!
All invalid neighbours eliminated in 1 CPU cycle
before the expansion step even starts.
Instead of an unpredictable if (IsWord) branch:
If not a new word (is_new = 0), the next node
simply overwrites the slot! Marks 1 bit per node
so duplicate paths never add the same word twice.
Wrote all 8 surrounding squares every time,
tzcnt counts trailing zeros to find the
(Rare 3+ steps handled by a short loop)
If keep had 2 bits set, advance by +2.
Repeat for Next Path Length Until Queue Is Empty
Now that the search is done,
zero the bits for the words
